newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Reemtsma wins battle for Moldovan tobacco.
newsitem.headline: Reemtsma wins battle for Moldovan tobacco.

text.p: German tobacco firm Reemtsma has beaten British rival B.A.T Industries Plc in a fight to control Moldova's tobacco industry, a top Moldovan official said on Wednesday.
"The government has decided...to set up a joint venture with Germany's Reemtsma," Deputy Prime Minister Valeriu Bulgari told reporters.

The deal, if it goes through, will be Moldova's biggest foreign investment to date, roughly doubling the total level of foreign investment in the former Soviet republic, which lies between Romania and Ukraine, from around $50 million at present.

Last year the government, seeking to attract investors to Moldova and revive its once thriving but now decaying tobacco industry, announced a tender offering for sale a stake up to 60 percent in its tobacco industry.

Five of the world's largest tobacco companies --Rothmans, Philip Morris, Reynolds, Reemtsma and BAT -- were invited by the government to take part in the tender, but only Reemtsma Cigarettenfabriken GmbH, part of Tchibo Holding AG, and BAT accepted.
In the mid-1980s Moldova produced over 130,000 tonnes of tobacco a year, or up to 40 percent of all Soviet output. Tobacco made up over 16 percent of its budget revenues.
But due to the economic crisis and lack of finance output nosedived to a mere 25,000 tonnes last year.
Moldova's tobacco industry, which consists of a cigarette factory in the capital Chisinau and eight fermentation plants, is valued by international auditors at some $60 million.
It is still attractive for foreign investors seeking to reinforce their presence in the former Soviet Union, where Moldovan cigarettes have a large market.
"The government and Reemtsma are now working on a package of documents necessary to set up the joint venture," Bulgari, who was in charge of the tobacco tender committee, said.
He gave no details of the capital structure of the new venture.

But Bulgari has previously told several economic commissions of parliament that Reemtsma -- if it won with its offer of $59 million of direct investment -- would own a 60-percent stake in an company with a future capital of $98.3 million.
BAT was offering $50 million of direct investment, he said.
Reemtsma planned to invest $44 million to produce cigarettes and other products and another $15 million to upgrade tobacco cultivation. BAT had offered $40 million and $10 million, respectively.
Other government officials have said that Reemtsma pledged to raise the production of tobacco to 90,000 tonnes within five years. Of this amount, Moldova hopes to export annually over 80,000 tonnes.
Reemtsma also plans to produce annually up to 15 billion cigarettes. The Chisinau plant produces at present some nine billion cigarettes, including 1.5 billion American blend.
